content.text: {"title":"Two Players and a Parser: What `tomli.loads` Promises","premise":"A caller hands Tomli a TOML string — a document with two `[[players]]` records — and expects back a plain Python dict of builtin types, or a clean `TOMLDecodeError` if the document is malformed. Nothing else: no partial results, no custom classes, no surprises. The string is the protagonist; the story follows it from the public entry point, through the single-pass statement loop, into the nested dict that is handed back, and notes at every branch what would have happened had the input been hostile or merely wrong.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"Across the trust boundary","trace_lines":[2,15],"data_in":"__s = '\\n[[players]]\\nname = \"Lehtinen\"\\nnumber = 26\\n\\n[[players]]\\nname = \"Numminen\"\\nnumber = 27\\n', parse_float=<class 'float'>","data_out":"src (CRLF-normalized copy), pos=0, header=(), out=Output(NestedDict{}, Flags{}), parse_float=<class 'float'> (unwrapped)","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:152-178","src/tomli/_parser.py:293-331","src/tomli/_parser.py:783-801"],"inputs":["__s: the TOML document as str","parse_float: callable, default float"],"characters":["loads","Output","NestedDict","Flags","make_safe_parse_float","load"],"facts":["`loads` first does `__s.replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\")`; an AttributeError/TypeError there is re-raised as `TypeError(\"Expected str object, not '<qualname>'\")`, so non-str input (bytes, bool) fails fast and typed, not with a confusing AttributeError.","The spec-permitted CRLF→LF rewrite happens on the whole document, including inside string literals; the parser therefore never sees a bare \\r\\n.","`load` only reads the file and delegates to `loads`; a text-mode file object raises `TypeError(\"File must be opened in binary mode...\")`, which is how the UTF-8/universal-newlines guarantee is enforced.","`make_safe_parse_float` returns the `float` builtin unchanged when `parse_float is float` (an explicit optimization), so in this run no validation wrapper exists at all.","All parser state is local to the call: a fresh `Output` holding an empty `NestedDict` (the result dict) and an empty `Flags` (namespace bookkeeping). There is no module-level mutable state, so concurrent `loads` calls do not interfere.","The trace shows `make_safe_parse_float(<class 'float'>) → <class 'float'>` (lines 9-10) and two `skip_chars` calls before the first statement."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q1.1","question":"If the default `float` is handed back unwrapped, what actually stops a custom `parse_float` from injecting a dict or list into the parsed output?"},{"id":"q1.2","question":"Nothing here prevents the same table name appearing twice. Where is that checked, and what is allowed to repeat?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":2,"title":"Reading the header name","trace_lines":[16,26],"data_in":"src, pos=1 (just past the leading newline), first char '[', second char '['","data_out":"(10, ('players',)) — key parsed, position parked on the closing brackets","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:180-216","src/tomli/_parser.py:405-408","src/tomli/_parser.py:478-513","src/tomli/_parser.py:333-339"],"inputs":["src","pos=1"],"characters":["loads statement loop","create_list_rule","parse_key","parse_key_part","skip_chars","KEY_INITIAL_CHARS","MAX_KEY_PARTS"],"facts":["The statement loop dispatches on a single character: a key-initial char (bare chars plus quote and apostrophe) starts a key/value rule, `[` starts a table or array-of-tables depending on the next character, `#` is a comment, and anything else raises `TOMLDecodeError(\"Invalid statement\")`.","Reading the second char is guarded by try/except IndexError, so a document ending in a lone `[` does not crash — it falls into `create_dict_rule` and fails with a decode error.","`create_list_rule` advances past `[[` (pos 1 → 3 in the trace) before trimming whitespace.","`parse_key_part` accepts bare keys (`BARE_KEY_CHARS`), `'literal'` and \"basic\" quoted parts; anything else raises `TOMLDecodeError(\"Invalid initial character for a key part\")`.","`parse_key` loops on `.` separators and enforces `MAX_KEY_PARTS = sys.getrecursionlimit()`, raising `RecursionError` beyond that — a deliberate bound because `Flags.is_` is quadratic in key length (CHANGELOG 2.4.1).","Trace: `parse_key(pos=3)` → `(10, ('players',))`; the key is a tuple of str, the parser's canonical namespace identity."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q2.1","question":"A key tuple has been produced, but nothing has been written yet. What decides whether this namespace may legally be opened at all?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":3,"title":"Claiming the namespace, appending the record","trace_lines":[27,43],"data_in":"key=('players',), out with empty flags and empty data dict, pos=10","data_out":"(12, ('players',)); out.data.dict == {'players': [{}]}, flag EXPLICIT_NEST set on ('players',); statement tail consumed to pos 13","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:385-425","src/tomli/_parser.py:235-290","src/tomli/_parser.py:315-324","src/tomli/_parser.py:218-230","src/tomli/_parser.py:342-382"],"inputs":["key=('players',)","out: Output"],"characters":["Flags.is_","Flags.unset_all","Flags.set","NestedDict.append_nest_to_list","NestedDict.get_or_create_nest","skip_comment","skip_until"],"facts":["`create_list_rule` refuses only one thing up front: a FROZEN key (`Cannot mutate immutable namespace`). Its sibling `create_dict_rule` additionally refuses EXPLICIT_NEST (`Cannot declare {key} twice`) — this asymmetry is exactly why `[[players]]` may repeat while `[players]` may not.","`unset_all` drops every flag beneath the key so the newly appended list item starts with a clean namespace; `set(key, EXPLICIT_NEST, recursive=False)` immediately re-claims the key itself.","`append_nest_to_list` raises `KeyError` if something other than a list already lives at the key; `create_list_rule` converts that to `TOMLDecodeError(\"Cannot overwrite a value\")`, so a type clash is a decode error, never a leaked KeyError.","After the key, `src.startswith(\"]]\", pos)` must hold, else `TOMLDecodeError(\"Expected ']]' at the end of an array declaration\")`.","The statement tail is uniform for every rule: trailing whitespace, then `skip_comment`, then `src[pos]` must be `\\n` or EOF, else `TOMLDecodeError(\"Expected newline or end of document after a statement\")`.","`skip_comment` delegates to `skip_until`, which scans to the next newline, tolerates EOF, but raises `Found invalid character ...` if an ASCII control char (ILLEGAL_COMMENT_CHARS) appears in the comment."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q3.1","question":"EXPLICIT_NEST was set, but `Flags.is_` was asked about FROZEN. What creates FROZEN namespaces, and what do they forbid?"},{"id":"q3.2","question":"`finalize_pending` ran and did nothing. What are pending flags for, and when do they bite?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q2.1","answer":"`Flags` decides. `create_dict_rule` rejects a key already marked EXPLICIT_NEST or FROZEN; `create_list_rule` rejects only FROZEN, then clears and re-claims the key. So a table may be declared once, an array-of-tables header may repeat, and a namespace frozen by an inline table/array is closed to both."}]},{"n":4,"title":"A key, an equals sign, and a quoted string","trace_lines":[44,62],"data_in":"src, pos=13, header=('players',), parse_float=float, nest_lvl=0","data_out":"(30, ('name',), 'Lehtinen')","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:428-431","src/tomli/_parser.py:462-518","src/tomli/_parser.py:703-776","src/tomli/_parser.py:671-700"],"inputs":["src","pos=13","nest_lvl=0"],"characters":["key_value_rule","parse_key_value_pair","parse_value","parse_one_line_basic_str","parse_basic_str","MAX_INLINE_NESTING"],"facts":["`parse_key_value_pair` re-uses the same `parse_key`, then demands `=` (after whitespace) or raises `TOMLDecodeError(\"Expected '=' after a key in a key/value pair\")`; a missing value at EOF ends in `parse_value` seeing char None and raising `Invalid value (at end of document)`.","`parse_value` dispatch order is documented as speed/likelihood-ordered: `\"`, `'`, `true`/`false`, `[`, `{`, then the datetime/localtime/number regexes, then inf/nan, then `TOMLDecodeError(\"Invalid value\")`.","`nest_lvl` enters at 0 and is incremented only for arrays and inline tables; `MAX_INLINE_NESTING = 400` raises `RecursionError` before mypyc-compiled builds can hit an unrecoverable stack overflow — a safety net for the binary wheels, not for pure Python.","`parse_basic_str` raises `TOMLDecodeError(\"Unterminated string\")` on EOF, `Illegal character {c!r}` for ASCII control chars (ILLEGAL_BASIC_STR_CHARS excludes tab), and resolves escapes through `BASIC_STR_ESCAPE_REPLACEMENTS` plus `\\x`/`\\u`/`\\U` hex forms validated as Unicode scalar values.","Trace: `parse_basic_str(pos=21, multiline=False)` → `(30, 'Lehtinen')`; the value is a plain `str`, as the README's type table promises."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q4.1","question":"There are now two possible homes for this value if more `[[players]]` blocks appear. Which dict actually receives `name`?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":5,"title":"Where the value is allowed to land","trace_lines":[63,73],"data_in":"key=('name',), value='Lehtinen', header=('players',), pos=30","data_out":"pos 30 returned; out.data.dict == {'players': [{'name': 'Lehtinen'}]}; statement tail consumed to pos 31","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:428-459","src/tomli/_parser.py:298-313","src/tomli/_parser.py:248-254"],"inputs":["key, value, header, out"],"characters":["key_value_rule","Flags.is_","Flags.add_pending","NestedDict.get_or_create_nest","Flags.set (FROZEN)"],"facts":["`abs_key_parent = header + key[:-1]` = `('players',)`; the value is written into the table named by the current header, never anywhere else.","For every intermediate container of a dotted key, `key_value_rule` errors if EXPLICIT_NEST is already set (`Cannot redefine namespace`) and otherwise records a *pending* EXPLICIT_NEST. With the single-part key `('name',)` the generator `range(1, len(key))` is empty, which is why the trace shows no `add_pending` call.","`Flags.is_(('players',), FROZEN)` → False permits the write; a True here would raise `Cannot mutate immutable namespace`.","`get_or_create_nest(..., access_lists=True)` walks the key and, whenever it meets a list, descends into `cont[-1]` — the most recently appended item. That single line is what makes `[[players]]` semantics work.","A `KeyError` from `get_or_create_nest` (a non-dict in the path) becomes `TOMLDecodeError(\"Cannot overwrite a value\")`; a key already present in the target dict raises the same error, so duplicate keys are rejected rather than silently overwritten.","If the value were a dict or list (inline table/array), `out.flags.set(header + key, FROZEN, recursive=True)` would close that whole subtree to later mutation — the guarantee behind `inline-table/mutate.toml` being invalid."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q3.1","answer":"FROZEN is set here, recursively, whenever a parsed value is a dict or list — i.e. for inline tables and arrays. It makes that namespace immutable: later `[a.b]`, `[[a.b]]` or dotted-key writes into it raise `Cannot mutate immutable namespace`."},{"id":"q4.1","answer":"The last element of the list. `get_or_create_nest` with `access_lists=True` steps into `cont[-1]`, so values after an `[[players]]` header always land in the item that header just appended — in this trace, the `{}` returned at line 66."}]},{"n":6,"title":"When the value is not a string: regexes, lazily","trace_lines":[74,95],"data_in":"src, pos=31 → key/value `number = 26`","data_out":"(42, ('number',), 26); out.data.dict == {'players': [{'name': 'Lehtinen', 'number': 26}]}","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:1-20","src/tomli/_parser.py:749-776","src/tomli/_re.py:26-56","src/tomli/_re.py:116-119"],"inputs":["src","pos=40 for the value"],"characters":["parse_value","RE_DATETIME","RE_LOCALTIME","RE_NUMBER","match_to_number","parse_float"],"facts":["`tomli._re` is declared in `__lazy_modules__` and is only touched when a value is not a string, bool, array or inline table — a deliberate import-time optimization (CHANGELOG 2.3.0), verified by `test_lazy_import`.","`RE_DATETIME` and `RE_LOCALTIME` are tried before `RE_NUMBER` because the number regex would greedily swallow the leading digits of `1987-07-05`; the comment at line 761-763 states this ordering requirement.","A string that matches `RE_DATETIME` but is not a real date (e.g. 2100-02-29) raises `ValueError` in `match_to_datetime`, which `parse_value` converts to `TOMLDecodeError(\"Invalid date or datetime\")` — calendar validity comes from `datetime`, not from the regex.","`match_to_number` branches on the named `floatpart` group: with a fractional or exponent part it calls `parse_float(text)`, otherwise `int(match.group(), 0)`, which accepts the `0x`/`0o`/`0b` prefixes and underscores the regex already validated.","Trace: `match_to_number(<Match span=(40,42) '26'>, float)` → `26` (an `int`), and `parse_value` returns `(42, 26)`.","Only after all regexes fail does the parser test the literal prefixes `inf`/`nan` and their signed four-char forms; failing that, `TOMLDecodeError(\"Invalid value\")`."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q6.1","question":"`int(group, 0)` will happily build an arbitrarily large integer from an arbitrarily long literal. Is anything in this design bounded by input size?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.1","answer":"Only the wrapper from `make_safe_parse_float`. A custom `parse_float` is called through `safe_parse_float`, which raises `ValueError(\"parse_float must not return dicts or lists\")` before the value can reach the output tree. Because `float` is special-cased and returned bare, the default path pays nothing — and needs nothing, since `float` cannot return those types."},{"id":"q5.1","answer":"Every failure in value parsing surfaces as `TOMLDecodeError`, a `ValueError` subclass carrying `msg`, `doc`, `pos`, `lineno`, `colno` and a formatted message like `Invalid value (at line 1, column 5)`. The README states the message text is informational only and not stable across versions, so callers should branch on the exception type and attributes, never on the string."}]},{"n":7,"title":"The same header again — legally","trace_lines":[96,126],"data_in":"src, pos=42; out.data.dict == {'players': [{'name': 'Lehtinen', 'number': 26}]}","data_out":"(55, ('players',)); out.data.dict == {'players': [{...26}, {}]}, header reset to ('players',)","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:204-214","src/tomli/_parser.py:248-273","src/tomli/_parser.py:405-425","src/tomli/_parser.py:315-324"],"inputs":["src","pos=44","out"],"characters":["Flags.finalize_pending","create_list_rule","Flags.unset_all","Flags.set","NestedDict.append_nest_to_list"],"facts":["`out.flags.finalize_pending()` is called before every `[`-headed rule, turning dotted-key container keys recorded earlier into real EXPLICIT_NEST flags and then clearing the pending set. This run has none pending, so it is a no-op (trace line 103-104).","The deferral exists so that a dotted key/value pair inside the *current* table does not block itself, while still closing those containers to later `[table]` or dotted-key reopening — the rule behind the invalid fixtures `dotted-keys/extend-defined-table.toml` and `table/append-with-dotted-keys-*.toml`.","`unset_all(('players',))` wipes the subtree of flags, which is what lets the second record use the key `name` again without tripping the duplicate check; `set(..., EXPLICIT_NEST)` immediately forbids a later `[players]`.","`append_nest_to_list` finds the existing list (trace line 123-124 shows the root dict already containing one record) and appends a fresh `{}`; the parser's notion of \"current record\" is simply `list[-1]`.","`create_list_rule` returns `(55, ('players',))` and `loads` assigns that key to `header`, which every following key/value statement will prefix."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q7.1","question":"Flags, pending sets and nested dicts have accumulated. What exactly does the caller receive at the end, and is it theirs?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.2","answer":"`[[players]]` may repeat by design: `create_list_rule` checks only FROZEN, then `unset_all` frees the namespace and appends a new item. A duplicate `[players]` table header, or a `[players]` after this, would hit the EXPLICIT_NEST flag set here and raise `Cannot declare ('players',) twice`."},{"id":"q3.2","answer":"Pending flags are EXPLICIT_NEST marks for the implicit containers created by dotted keys. They are held back until the next `[`-headed statement so the current table can keep writing into them, then `finalize_pending` commits them — after which reopening those containers with table syntax is an error."}]},{"n":8,"title":"The second record, and handing back the dict","trace_lines":[127,191],"data_in":"src, pos=55, header=('players',), out.data.dict == {'players': [{...26}, {}]}","data_out":"{'players': [{'name': 'Lehtinen', 'number': 26}, {'name': 'Numminen', 'number': 27}]}","code":["src/tomli/_parser.py:180-232","src/tomli/_parser.py:428-459","src/tomli/_parser.py:298-313"],"inputs":["src","pos=55..86"],"characters":["key_value_rule","parse_basic_str","match_to_number","NestedDict.get_or_create_nest","loads loop exit"],"facts":["The two remaining statements retrace chapters 4-6 exactly: `name` → `parse_one_line_basic_str` → `(73, 'Numminen')`, `number` → `RE_NUMBER` → `match_to_number` → `27`.","Both land in the second record because `get_or_create_nest(('players',))` returns `cont[-1]`: the trace shows it returning `{}` at line 155 and `{'name': 'Numminen'}` at line 183.","The loop exits where `src[pos]` raises IndexError at EOF (line 194-197 or 222-225), so a document ending in a newline, whitespace, or nothing at all terminates cleanly without an error.","`loads` returns `out.data.dict` directly — the parser's own dict, not a copy. The caller owns a plain `dict` of builtins and stdlib datetime types; `Flags` and all pending state are simply dropped with the stack frame.","Parsing is single-pass over one in-memory string with integer positions and slicing; there is no streaming mode, so peak memory is proportional to document size, and no timeout or size cap exists at this layer.","`out.data.dict` is mutable and shared with nothing else; concurrent callers each get their own `Output`, so the returned value is safe to mutate."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q6.1","answer":"Only key depth and inline nesting are bounded (`MAX_KEY_PARTS`, `MAX_INLINE_NESTING = 400`); document length, individual literal length and integer digit count are not. A pathological numeric literal is bounded only by CPython's own int↔str digit limit, which raises ValueError rather than TOMLDecodeError — worth knowing before parsing untrusted input without a size cap of your own."},{"id":"q7.1","answer":"A plain `dict` containing only `str`, `int`, `float` (or whatever `parse_float` returned), `bool`, `datetime`/`date`/`time`, `list` and `dict`. It is the parser's internal dict handed over whole, not copied, and all bookkeeping state is discarded; the caller may mutate it freely."}]}]}
